en: The Essential Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Most Extraordinary and Supreme Golden Wheel Uṣṇīṣa:
For those who wish to practice the Dharma of the One-Syllable Cakravartin King, they must first enter the Great Maṇḍala.
In the ocean-like assembly,
one receives the empowerment directly from the master;
only after having received this seal of approval may one then seek instruction.
One should study the subtle rules and the gateway of mantra teachings,
and establish a maṇḍala strictly according to the ritual procedures of the respective family (kula).
Paint an image of the principal deity and install it according to the ritual rules.
If you wish to swiftly accomplish siddhi, [proceed as follows].
First, one must bathe and put on new, clean clothes;
if one is a renunciant, [one should do so as well].
One should maintain the vows of discipline with diligence and must not allow them to be deficient or transgressed.
This applies even for those who remain householders.
One should receive the eightfold pure precepts of the upavāsa,
and furthermore, one should earnestly and respectfully generate a vast mind,
regarding the ācārya with veneration as if he were a Buddha.
Out of compassion for all sentient beings, they give rise to the vow of great pity;
disregarding their own bodies and lives, they constantly manifest to deliver them,
causing all to be free from suffering and attain great benefit and happiness.
Having entered the maṇḍala,
one prostrates with the five limbs touching the ground and reverently pays homage to all the Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, facing the Honored One and the assembly of holy beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, one purifies the three karmas to repent and eliminate karmic obstructions,
and entreats all Buddhas to turn the wondrous Wheel of Dharma.
I rejoice in the merit and wisdom cultivated by those of the three vehicles.
With these sublime virtues, I dedicate them toward enlightenment,
so that all sentient beings within the dharma realm may together ascend to the fruit of Buddhahood.
Next, apply scented ointment to the hands,
join the palms like a lotus,
and contemplate the fundamental source.
Having made this contemplation that the naturally pure [mind] is obscured by adventitious defilements, [one proceeds].
Extending the mind universally:
"I and all sentient beings are likewise pure;
for the sake of bringing about this purity."
Recite this supreme mantra for bathing:
Oṃ sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhānena svāhā. By reciting this vidyā three times.
The three karmas of body, speech, and mind, extending throughout the entire dharma realm, are all completely purified.
Next, bind the Samaya Seal of the Mind of the Family of All Buddhas:
form the fists with the hands crossed at the palms, representing the ten perfections within śamatha and vipaśyanā.
Joining the two mudrās of dhyāna and prajñā together,
one surveys all Buddhas filling the entirety of space;
reciting the mantra three times, one disperses the mudrā above the crown of the head.
The heart mantra of the Buddhas family is:
Oṃ īrṇīrka svāhā. By binding the aforementioned mudrā and reciting this mantra, [the rite is accomplished].
The Buddhas of the ten directions, all the Tathāgatas,
by virtue of their original vows,
have all gathered and assembled here.
Pervading the entirety of space,
they extend their light to illuminate and empower the practitioner.
Free from all obstacles and afflictions,
with the three karmas purified,
they shall swiftly realize Bodhi.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Heart of the Lotus Family of all Bodhisattvas.
Perform this according to the previous method for binding the Heart-mudrā of the Buddha Family:

bend the left *jñāna-sūtra* (index finger) into the palm, extend the *dhyāna-sūtra* (middle finger) straight upward, or perform three beckoning gestures. Direct the mind to recollect and visualize Avalokiteśvara.
All the hosts of Bodhisattvas as numerous as atoms, holding lotuses and accompanied by their retinues, fill the sky.
Recite the mantra with a sincere mind three times, and then apply the mudrā to the crown of the head, scattering [the flowers].
The Heart Mantra of the Lotus Family is as follows:
Oṃ arulika phaṭ svāhā. By binding the aforementioned mudrā and reciting this mantra, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, in accordance with his original vow, [responds].
He brought together and gathered all the various lotuses and immeasurable bodhisattvas,
filling the entirety of space.
Emitting great radiance,
they empower the practitioner,
causing them to attain purity.
May all their aspirations be fulfilled,
may they be free from all obstacles and difficulties,
and may they swiftly realize bodhi.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Heart of the Sarva-vajra-kula.
Following the previous procedure, again bind the Heart-mudrā of the Buddha-kula:
bend the right *dhyāna-aṅguli* (ring finger) into the palm; extend the *prajñā-aṅguli* (index finger) straight upward, or perform three beckoning gestures.
Surrounded by a retinue as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, his majestic radiance pervades the entirety of space.
Having recited the mantra three times with utmost sincerity, one should then apply the mudrā to the crown of the head;
the heart-mantra of the Vajra Family for scattering to the left is as follows:
Oṃ vajra-dhṛk phaṭ svāhā. By binding the aforementioned mudrā and reciting this mantra, all Vajrapāṇis and others throughout the ten directions, by virtue of their original vows, [respond].
They gather like clouds,
manifesting great majestic power and bestowing their empowerment upon the practitioner.
Eliminating obstacles and subduing māras,
one attains sovereign unimpededness and swiftly accomplishes siddhi.
One swiftly attains enlightenment.
Next, bind the seal for protecting the body with the Vajra Armor:
form vajra fists with the thumbs and ring fingers as feathers, and cross the middle and index fingers within the palms.
The advancing force is like a hook, with the momentum of armored power. Recite the mantra three times over the heart, forehead, two shoulders, and throat.
The mantra for donning the armor and protecting the body by sealing the five places of the body and scattering [the mudrā] above the crown is as follows:
Oṃ jvala hūṃ. By reciting this mantra while forming the armor mudrā,
one consecrates the five places and achieves great protection of the body.
He is identical to a body as firm and solid as a vajra.
Vajragarbha-rāja, by virtue of his original vow,
leads all his retinues.
Surrounded and attended by immeasurable vajra-holders as numerous as dust motes and sand grains,
his radiance was blazing and intense,
and he manifested in a wrathful form.
The practitioner is empowered,
possessing majestic virtue and sovereign power,
and is cleared of all obstacles.
It destroys all demons;
on a small scale, it can protect a single person,
and on a large scale, it protects and sustains the boundaries of a nation.
All calamities and misfortunes—
water, fire, weapons, and warfare;
poisons, sorcery, tigers, wolves, and fierce beasts.
They all remained far removed from it, not daring to look upon it;
Vināyakas naturally fled in fear,
and there was never again any affliction or harm.
Swiftly realize enlightenment.
Next, bind the Seal for Accomplishing Affairs:

with the two hands of śamatha and vipaśyanā, clasp them into fists with the fingers interlaced, and bend both the wisdom-fingers (middle fingers) and the dhyāna-fingers (ring fingers) inward into the palms.

Then, extending the hands of patience and aspiration with the heads touching, one performs three rotations on the crown of the head to form a protective seal; turning three times to the left is for expulsion. According to where the mind reaches, one establishes the directions and corners; this *dharmapada* can accomplish all matters. *Namo samantabuddhānām oṃ nṛ-maṇḍa svāhā.* By forming the aforementioned mudrā and reciting this mantra, [the rite is accomplished].
It is fully capable of expelling [obstacles] and binding and protecting the boundary.
This is called the Buddhas’ awakening of the noble mind,
which is able to destroy the teachings of others.
He destroys Māra,
the eight classes of devas and nāgas,
rākṣasas, and yakṣas.
The Vināyakas flee in terror and haste because of the binding of this mudrā.
All worldly and world-transcending undertakings will be swiftly accomplished;
one will attain mastery and unimpededness,
and *siddhi* will manifest before them.
Next, perform the mudrā for offering argha:
with both hands palms upturned, form the shape of a vessel;

bend the vajra and wisdom fingers (tarjanī and jyeṣṭhā) alongside the earth and pledge fingers (anāmikā and kaniṣṭhā), and curve the meditation and intellect fingers (madhyamā and aṅguṣṭha) to touch the vajra and wisdom fingers.
Holding the vessel, rotate it three times above the forehead and visualize the assembly of noble ones being bathed as pure as a lotus.
The *udaka* (consecrated water) bathing mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ āgana-saṃśodhana svāhā*. By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra, one offers the *udaka* for the bathing of the noble ones.
This manifests that the defiled karma of the practitioner from beginningless time is washed away and purified,
like a wondrous lotus flower;
in the future, the fruit will be the attainment of untainted wisdom.
Next, bind the mudrā of the Universal Offering to Space:
Join the two palms and interlace the first phalanges; with the right hand pressing over the left, form the bond as if visualizing a vajra.
This constitutes the truly sublime and wondrous offering, which is presented as an immeasurable ocean of clouds to the assembly of holy ones.

Having made offerings to all the Tathāgatas, one then recites these four lines of sublime gāthās five times and recites the Great Illumination Mantra while scattering [flowers] into the sky above the crown of the head. The mantra is: Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | sarvatha khaṃ maṇḍale hīma gaganakhe svāhā || By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, [the rite is accomplished].
By means of inconceivable power,
all manner of offerings flow forth from the mudrā;
immeasurable hosts of devas each hold celestial jewel vessels.
They prepared various sublime offerings that filled the entirety of space— namely, scented unguents, burning lamps,
food, drink, and clothing.
By offering banners, canopies,
and necklaces to the Tathāgata and reciting this once,
ointment incense flows forth.
In the future, one shall obtain the fragrant ointment of the aggregate of ethical discipline (*śīlaskandha*).
Because the mantra is recited twice,
incense flows forth.
In the future, one will obtain the fragrance of meditative concentration;
by reciting this three times,
flower garlands will flow forth.
In the future, one shall obtain the sublime lotus free from defilement;
by reciting this four times,
precious food will flow forth.
In the future, one shall obtain the joy of the Dharma and the bliss of dhyāna;
by reciting this five times,
precious lamps will flow forth.
In the future, they shall obtain the five eyes of a Tathāgata.
They shall attain and become fully endowed with all the aforementioned gates of merit and pāramitās.
Furthermore, their minds shall pervade the entire Dharma-realm.
Reciting a sublime gāthā with truthful words,
he spoke this verse:
"By the power of my merit and by the power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment..."
And by the power of the dharmadhātu, one dwells while making universal offerings;
next, one praises with Brahma-like hymns the sublime qualities of the deity’s golden body and its excellent marks and signs.
Māṇe mani sarvajñāgrye dadi svāhini pūḥ pūrvaṃ nigamaṃ dhāraya samasta-vinyastebhyaḥ kramālini namo'stu te tārataraja-kramavartini. (I praise the Buddha’s three bodies.)
The various merits of the six sense faculties,
numbering eighty-four thousand kinds,
are supreme and inconceivable.
By virtue of this cause of chanting and praise,
one shall obtain the wondrous fruit in the future;
the accumulation of merit will be as boundless as the ocean.
Equal to the wondrous and sublime Honored One,
next bind the Great Vidyā-mudrā of Buddhalocanā:
The thumbs and little fingers joined in equipoise without opening, the middle and ring fingers both bent within the palms.
Each with advancing strength, they press their palms together at the back;

as the eyes open with clarity, illuminating all, one places [the hand] on the brow-center, the forehead, the two shoulders, and the throat. Arising with great compassion, one removes fear while reciting the mantra, and finally disperses it above the crown of the head.
The mantra of the Great Vidyārājñī Buddha-eye is as follows:
*Namaḥ sarvatathāgatebhyo viyugma-viyoga-samyaksambuddhe oṃ ruru sphuru jvala tiṣṭha siddhalocane svāhā*. This is called the Great Vidyā of all Buddha-eyes.
It is able to pacify those who are fearsome and difficult to subdue.
It is intended for the accomplishment of all matters and stages of the mundane and supramundane Great Wheel-King Dhāraṇī of the Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa, and for the extinguishing of all disputes.
It is also the mother of the lineage of all Buddhas,
and further, the mother who gives birth to and nurtures all the great Bodhisattvas;
it proclaims the extraordinary majesty and power of the Uṣṇīṣa mantra.
All the great bodhisattvas lose their original minds,
and the majestic powers of all devas, nāgas, and spirits vanish;
this applies to anyone who recites even a single syllable of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa vidyā-mantra.
First, one must recite the Buddha-eye mantra (*Buddhalocanā-vidyā*).
Once the recitation is completed,
one should likewise recite it seven times.
May the assembly of noble ones rejoice and bring peace and happiness to sentient beings.
Next, bind the One-Syllable Root Mudrā:
with the hands of *śamatha* and *vipaśyanā* tightly bound, cross the fists within; by means of the *kuśa*, *kṣānti*, *praṇidhāna*, and *praṇidhi* fingers, form the shape of a sword.
With the power of meditative wisdom and diligence, the armor-clad pillar is firmly planted; this is called the visualization of the Vajra-uṣṇīṣa-mudrā.

Its majestic majesty is identical to that of the Honored One [the Buddha]; radiant light flows forth, pervading the ten directions, as it is scattered upon the five places of the body and the crown of the head.
The mantra of the Sovereign of the Golden Wheel Crown is as follows:
This is the Mahāmudrā, namely the Tathāgata’s Crown;
by binding it and reciting it, one becomes identical to the World-Honored One.
He proclaimed the Vidyā of Uṣṇīṣa; with three thousand six hundred recitations, the mountains and rivers shook and seethed with vigor.
Great fires spread throughout the palaces of Māra, who, struck with terror, all took refuge;
the manifold sufferings of the hells were stilled.
The assembly of Bodhisattvas, nāgas, and devas revere and look up [at him] as if he were the body of a Buddha.
Next, bind the seal of Great Compassionate Universal Protection (*mahāmaitrī-sarvarakṣā-mudrā*).

Interlace the fingers of the ten hands to form the shape of a crescent moon; join the thumbs (*tarjanī*) and the wisdom-fingers (*jñāna-aṅguli*) together. Place the seal upon the heart, forehead, throat, and crown of the head. The mantra for the dispersal of compassionate protection is as follows: [Mantra follows]
Forming mudrās and reciting mantras, one dispels fear; Arousing the mind of great compassion, one pervades all enemies and malevolent forms with it.
May they all attain great peace and happiness through these three recitations of compassionate protection; Thus, their poisonous and harmful minds will naturally awaken.
Deeply repenting of transgressions, one turns toward Bodhi; with joy and reverence, one honors those who came before.

If one constantly recites this mantra at the beginning and the end, sentient beings filled with fear will find solace, and through this great protection, they will attain extraordinary benefits and swiftly fulfill all aspirations, realizing *siddhi*.
Next, form the mudrā of the pure jewel:
place the beads within the palms in the shape of an unopened lotus, and hold them joined at the heart; empower them twenty-one times.
Wearing [the rosary] upon the crown of the head with a heart of earnest devotion, one should perform the offering according to the ritual.
The mantra for the pure rosary is:
OṂ ĀḤ HRĪḤ TĪKṢṆE JVALITE SIDDHISIDDHAYE TIṢṬHA SVĀHĀ. Next, one should form the mudrā for counting the recitations.
With the two hands in the half-vajra gesture, join the thumbs and index fingers (the wisdom fingers) at the square of the wrists (the precept fingers),
and bend the remaining fingers— forefingers, middle fingers, ring fingers, and little fingers— so that they do not touch one another. Recite the vidyā-mantra seven times,
and thereafter perform the recitation.
The mantra for holding the jewel is as follows:
First, one should purify the three karmas; then, recite with the addition of the mudrā, single-mindedly without distraction, while fixing the visualization upon the deity.
Recite the words and phrases clearly; neither too slow nor too fast, do not give rise to thoughts of indolence.
Even if interrupted by coughing, yawning, or the defilements of mental dullness—such are the various faults.
If one occasionally experiences forgetfulness, one must not continue until the recitation count is completed;
once the mantra has been held and the rosary returned to its original place,
one may then enter the samaya and abide in the visualization of the deity.
After a meal’s duration, emerge from meditative absorption; Then, re-form the root mudrā and next form the Buddha-eye mantra.
Having offered praise with melodic chanting and performed the universal offering of argha, Dispel obstacles by releasing the mudrā with the left hand.
Perform the threefold protection of the body; finally, perform the mudrā of compassionate protection and the rite of confession according to the previous protocol.
Recite Mahāyāna scriptures as you wish, whether walking or sitting, and do not let this practice be interrupted at any time.

*The Essential Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Supreme and Extraordinary Golden Wheel Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa*, one fascicle. If one is unable to recite the aforementioned Great Buddha-Eye Mantra, it is also permissible to recite this Heart Mantra; this is the Minor Buddha-Eye Spell.
Namo samantabuddhānām | Oṃ mūrdha locana lalita svāhā. Regarding the ritual for the water mandala: take fresh, pure cow dung.
One must not eat dregs, beans, or fodder;
the dung of a calf is the very best.
One must not use raw cow dung directly.
Take a new earthen jar to draw pure water;
do not use leftover water,
and pour it into the vessel for pure water.
Mix the excrement with water,
stir it to remove the dregs,
and add powdered sandalwood.
Take a willow branch and hold it with the right hand;
hold a vajra and a rosary with the left hand.
Sitting facing east, recite the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī while stirring water with a willow branch;
recite it one hundred and eight times.
Holding the water vessel for recitation,
enter the maṇḍala and draw up the fragrant water from the northeast corner.
He rubbed the ground with his right hand,
moving in the direction of the sun's course;
as he rubbed it, it dried up accordingly.
Do not allow the water to stagnate.
Once the ground within the site of practice has been rubbed once over,
continue until the water at the four sides of the site has also been rubbed.
Mark each step of the ground with four corner markers, erecting stakes and binding them with ropes to form the boundary.
This is called the site for binding the boundaries through the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa-samādhi-dhāraṇī,
as described in a single fascicle.
The second and third [applications] are likewise rubbed.
One must not use leftover scented water for the *mārjanā*;
one should take fresh, pure cow dung separately each day.
Proceed as previously described.
When this water has been prepared, it is called the "Eight Virtues Water" of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa Samādhi Dhāraṇī; the consecration of the ritual ground is now complete.
